sanskrit: bhāṇḍāgārāyudhāgārān dhānyāgārāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ aśvāgārān gajāgārān balādhikaraṇāni ca
english: The storehouses, the armories, and the granaries of every kind, the stables for horses and the stalls for elephants, and the headquarters of the army—

sanskrit: parikhāś caiva kauravya pratolīḥ saṃkaṭāni ca na jātu kaś cit paśyet tu guhyam etad yudhiṣṭhira
english: the moats too, O Kaurava, the broad roads and the narrow passes—let no one ever look upon these, for they are secret matters, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: atha saṃnicayaṃ kuryād rājā parabalārditaḥ tailaṃ madhu ghṛtaṃ sasyam auṣadhāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then a king hard pressed by an enemy's forces should lay up stores—oil, honey, clarified butter, grain, and medicines of every kind.

sanskrit: aṅgārakuśamuñjānāṃ palāśaśaraparṇinām yavasendhanadigdhānāṃ kārayeta ca saṃcayān
english: Of charcoal, of kuśa and muñja grass, of the leaves of palāśa and reed, and of fodder, fuel, and resin, let him have stocks gathered up.

sanskrit: āyudhānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śaktyṛṣṭiprāsavarmaṇām saṃcayān evamādīnāṃ kārayeta narādhipaḥ
english: And of weapons of every sort—lances, swords, javelins, and armor—and of such things, let the lord of men have stores laid by.

sanskrit: auṣadhāni ca sarvāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca caturvidhāṃś ca vaidyān vai saṃgṛhṇīyād viśeṣataḥ
english: All medicines too, with their roots and fruits, and physicians of the four kinds, he should especially keep at hand.

sanskrit: naṭāś ca nartakāś caiva mallā māyāvinas tathā śobhayeyuḥ puravaraṃ modayeyuś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Actors and dancers, wrestlers and conjurers as well, should adorn the fair city and gladden the people in every way.

sanskrit: yataḥ śaṅkā bhavec cāpi bhṛtyato vāpi mantritaḥ paurebhyo nṛpater vāpi svādhīnān kārayeta tān
english: And wherever suspicion may arise—whether of a servant or of a counselor, of the townsfolk or even of the king himself—he should keep those persons under his own control.

sanskrit: kṛte karmaṇi rājendra pūjayed dhanasaṃcayaiḥ mānena ca yathārheṇa sāntvena vividhena ca
english: When a task is accomplished, O lord of kings, he should honor men with gifts of wealth, with fitting marks of esteem, and with kind words of many kinds.

sanskrit: nirvedayitvā tu paraṃ hatvā vā kurunandana gatānṛṇyo bhaved rājā yathā śāstreṣu darśitam
english: Having driven off the enemy or slain him, O joy of the Kurus, the king becomes free of his debt, as is shown in the scriptures.

sanskrit: rājñā saptaiva rakṣyāṇi tāni cāpi nibodha me ātmāmātyaś ca kośaś ca daṇḍo mitrāṇi caiva hi
english: Seven things are to be guarded by a king; learn them from me: his own self, his ministers, his treasury, his armed force, and his allies,

sanskrit: tathā janapadaś caiva puraṃ ca kurunandana etat saptātmakaṃ rājyaṃ paripālyaṃ prayatnataḥ
english: and likewise his realm and his capital, O joy of the Kurus. This sevenfold kingdom must be protected with diligence.

sanskrit: ṣāḍguṇyaṃ ca trivargaṃ ca trivargam aparaṃ tathā yo vetti puruṣavyāghra sa bhunakti mahīm imām
english: The sixfold policy, the triad of aims, and the other triad besides—he who knows these, O tiger among men, enjoys this earth.

sanskrit: ṣāḍguṇyam iti yat proktaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira saṃdhāyāsanam ity eva yātrāsaṃdhānam eva ca
english: What is called the sixfold policy, learn that now, O Yudhiṣṭhira: making peace and then staying still; marching forth after concluding an alliance;

sanskrit: vigṛhyāsanam ity eva yātrāṃ saṃparigṛhya ca dvaidhībhāvas tathānyeṣāṃ saṃśrayo 'tha parasya ca
english: waging war and then staying still; setting out on a campaign; the policy of division among others; and taking refuge with a stronger power.

sanskrit: trivargaś cāpi yaḥ proktas tam ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu kṣayaḥ sthānaṃ ca vṛddhiś ca trivargam aparaṃ tathā
english: And the triad that has been spoken of—hear it now with single mind: decline, stability, and growth; that is the one triad.

sanskrit: dharmaś cārthaś ca kāmaś ca sevitavyo 'tha kālataḥ dharmeṇa hi mahīpālaś ciraṃ pālayate mahīm
english: Dharma, profit, and pleasure—these are to be pursued, each in its proper season; for it is through dharma that the protector of the earth governs the earth for long.

sanskrit: asminn arthe ca yau ślokau gītāv aṅgirasā svayam yādavīputra bhadraṃ te śrotum arhasi tāv api
english: On this matter there are two verses sung by Aṅgiras himself; O son of the Yādava woman, blessings upon you—it is fitting that you hear these too.

sanskrit: kṛtvā sarvāṇi kāryāṇi samyak saṃpālya medinīm pālayitvā tathā paurān paratra sukham edhate
english: Having performed all his duties, having well protected the earth, and having guarded his people, he flourishes in happiness in the world beyond.

sanskrit: kiṃ tasya tapasā rājñaḥ kiṃ ca tasyādhvarair api apālitāḥ prajā yasya sarvā dharmavinākṛtāḥ
english: What use is austerity to that king, and what use his sacrifices, whose subjects, left unprotected, are all bereft of dharma?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca daṇḍanītiś ca rājā ca samastau tāv ubhāv api kasya kiṃ kurvataḥ siddhyai tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The science of punishment and the king—the two taken together, both of them—through whose doing of what does success come about? Tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mahābhāgyaṃ daṇḍanītyāḥ siddhaiḥ śabdaiḥ sahetukaiḥ śṛṇu me śaṃsato rājan yathāvad iha bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear from me, O king, as I declare it duly here, O Bhārata, the great majesty of the science of punishment, in well-established words backed by reasons.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītiḥ svadharmebhyaś cāturvarṇyaṃ niyacchati prayuktā svāminā samyag adharmebhyaś ca yacchati
english: The science of punishment, rightly applied by the lord, keeps the four orders to their own duties, and holds them back from acts contrary to dharma.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇye svadharmasthe maryādānām asaṃkare daṇḍanītikṛte kṣeme prajānām akutobhaye
english: When the four orders abide each in its own duty, when the bounds of conduct are unconfused, when the science of punishment has wrought security and the people have nothing to fear from any quarter—

sanskrit: some prayatnaṃ kurvanti trayo varṇā yathāvidhi tasmād devamanuṣyāṇāṃ sukhaṃ viddhi samāhitam
english: then the three orders make their effort in the Soma rites as enjoined; know therefore that the happiness of gods and men alike rests secure upon this.

sanskrit: kālo vā kāraṇaṃ rājño rājā vā kālakāraṇam iti te saṃśayo mā bhūd rājā kālasya kāraṇam
english: Whether the age is the cause of the king, or the king is the cause of the age—let no such doubt remain in you: it is the king who is the cause of the age.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītyā yadā rājā samyak kārtsnyena vartate tadā kṛtayugaṃ nāma kālaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pravartate
english: When a king conducts himself by the science of punishment rightly and in its entirety, then sets in that best of ages named the Kṛta Yuga.

sanskrit: bhavet kṛtayuge dharmo nādharmo vidyate kva cit sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ nādharme ramate manaḥ
english: In the Kṛta age dharma prevails; nowhere is unrighteousness to be found; and among all the orders the mind takes no pleasure in unrighteousness.

sanskrit: yogakṣemāḥ pravartante prajānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ vaidikāni ca karmāṇi bhavanty aviguṇāny uta
english: The acquisition and keeping of goods proceed for the people—of this there is no doubt—and the rites enjoined by the Vedas come to pass without defect.

sanskrit: ṛtavaś ca sukhāḥ sarve bhavanty uta nirāmayāḥ prasīdanti narāṇāṃ ca svaravarṇamanāṃsi ca
english: All the seasons too are pleasant and free of sickness, and the voices, complexions, and minds of men grow serene.

sanskrit: vyādhayo na bhavanty atra nālpāyur dṛśyate naraḥ vidhavā na bhavanty atra nṛśaṃso nābhijāyate
english: No diseases arise then, nor is any man seen short-lived; no widows are there, and no cruel man is born.

sanskrit: akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī bhavanty oṣadhayas tathā tvakpatraphalamūlāni vīryavanti bhavanti ca
english: The earth yields its harvest without tillage, and so too do the plants spring up; bark, leaf, fruit, and root all become full of potency.

sanskrit: nādharmo vidyate tatra dharma eva tu kevalaḥ iti kārtayugān etān guṇān viddhi yudhiṣṭhira
english: No unrighteousness is found there, but dharma alone, entire. Know these to be the qualities of the Kṛta age, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītyā yadā rājā trīn aṃśān anuvartate caturtham aṃśam utsṛjya tadā tretā pravartate
english: When a king follows the science of punishment in three parts, letting the fourth part go, then the Tretā age sets in.

sanskrit: aśubhasya caturthāṃśas trīn aṃśān anuvartate kṛṣṭapacyaiva pṛthivī bhavanty oṣadhayas tathā
english: A fourth part of evil then attends upon the three parts of good; and the earth yields its harvest only when tilled, and so too the plants.

sanskrit: ardhaṃ tyaktvā yadā rājā nītyardham anuvartate tatas tu dvāparaṃ nāma sa kālaḥ saṃpravartate
english: When a king, abandoning half, follows but half of right policy, then sets in that age named the Dvāpara.

sanskrit: aśubhasya tadā ardhaṃ dvāv aṃśāv anuvartate kṛṣṭapacyaiva pṛthivī bhavaty alpaphalā tathā
english: Then half of evil attends upon the two parts of good; and the earth yields its harvest only when tilled, and that too with scant fruit.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītiṃ parityajya yadā kārtsnyena bhūmipaḥ prajāḥ kliśnāty ayogena praviśyati tadā kaliḥ
english: When the lord of the earth forsakes the science of punishment entirely and afflicts his people by misrule, then enters the Kali age.

sanskrit: kalāv adharmo bhūyiṣṭhaṃ dharmo bhavati tu kva cit sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ svadharmāc cyavate manaḥ
english: In the Kali age unrighteousness is most abundant, and dharma scarcely anywhere; and among all the orders the mind falls away from its own duty.

sanskrit: śūdrā bhaikṣeṇa jīvanti brāhmaṇāḥ paricaryayā yogakṣemasya nāśaś ca vartate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
english: Śūdras live by begging and Brāhmaṇas by menial service; the acquisition and keeping of goods is undone, and the confusion of orders prevails.

sanskrit: vaidikāni ca karmāṇi bhavanti viguṇāny uta ṛtavo nasukhāḥ sarve bhavanty āmayinas tathā
english: The rites enjoined by the Vedas are performed with defects, and all the seasons turn unpleasant and breed disease.

sanskrit: hrasanti ca manuṣyāṇāṃ svaravarṇamanāṃsy uta vyādhayaś ca bhavanty atra mriyante cāgatāyuṣaḥ
english: The voices, complexions, and minds of men diminish; diseases arise then, and men die before their span is full.

sanskrit: vidhavāś ca bhavanty atra nṛśaṃsā jāyate prajā kva cid varṣati parjanyaḥ kva cit sasyaṃ prarohati
english: Widows are found then, and the people are born cruel; in one place the rain-cloud pours, in another the grain springs up.

sanskrit: rasāḥ sarve kṣayaṃ yānti yadā necchati bhūmipaḥ prajāḥ saṃrakṣituṃ samyag daṇḍanītisamāhitaḥ
english: All the savors waste away to nothing—when the lord of the earth, intent upon the science of punishment, no longer wills to guard his people aright.

sanskrit: rājā kṛtayugasraṣṭā tretāyā dvāparasya ca yugasya ca caturthasya rājā bhavati kāraṇam
english: The king is the maker of the Kṛta age, and of the Tretā and the Dvāpara; the king is the cause of the fourth age as well.

sanskrit: kṛtasya karaṇād rājā svargam atyantam aśnute tretāyāḥ karaṇād rājā svargaṃ nātyantam aśnute
english: By bringing about the Kṛta age the king attains heaven unending; by bringing about the Tretā the king attains a heaven not unending.

sanskrit: pravartanād dvāparasya yathābhāgam upāśnute kaleḥ pravartanād rājā pāpam atyantam aśnute
english: By ushering in the Dvāpara he partakes of heaven in due measure; by ushering in the Kali the king reaps endless sin.

sanskrit: tato vasati duṣkarmā narake śāśvatīḥ samāḥ prajānāṃ kalmaṣe magno 'kīrtiṃ pāpaṃ ca vindati
english: Then the evildoer dwells in hell for everlasting years; sunk in the defilement of his people, he gains only infamy and sin.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītiṃ puraskṛtya vijānan kṣatriyaḥ sadā anavāptaṃ ca lipseta labdhaṃ ca paripālayet
english: Setting the science of punishment foremost, the discerning Kṣatriya should ever strive to gain what is not yet won, and to preserve what is won.

sanskrit: lokasya sīmantakarī maryādā lokabhāvanī samyaṅ nītā daṇḍanītir yathā mātā yathā pitā
english: Drawing the boundary lines of the world, fostering the world, the science of punishment well administered is as a mother and as a father.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ bhavanti bhūtāni tad viddhi bharatarṣabha eṣa eva paro dharmo yad rājā daṇḍanītimān
english: In her all beings have their being—know this, O bull of the Bhāratas. This is the supreme dharma: that the king be wielder of the science of punishment.

sanskrit: tasmāt kauravya dharmeṇa prajāḥ pālaya nītimān evaṃvṛttaḥ prajā rakṣan svargaṃ jetāsi durjayam
english: Therefore, O Kaurava, guard your people by dharma, skilled in policy; conducting yourself thus and protecting the people, you shall win that heaven hard to win.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kena vṛttena vṛttajña vartamāno mahīpatiḥ sukhenārthān sukhodarkān iha ca pretya cāpnuyāt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By what conduct, O knower of conduct, should the lord of the earth bear himself, that with ease he may attain ends fruitful in happiness, both here and after death?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca iyaṃ guṇānāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśat ṣaṭtriṃśad guṇasaṃyutā yān guṇāṃs tu guṇopetaḥ kurvan guṇam avāpnuyāt
english: Bhīṣma said: Here is the set of six-and-thirty virtues, joined with six-and-thirty merits; practicing these virtues, the man endowed with virtue gains the good thereof.

sanskrit: cared dharmān akaṭuko muñcet snehaṃ na nāstikaḥ anṛśaṃsaś cared arthaṃ caret kāmam anuddhataḥ
english: Let him follow the duties without harshness; let him let go of attachment, yet not become a denier; let him pursue profit without cruelty, and pursue pleasure without arrogance.

sanskrit: priyaṃ brūyād akṛpaṇaḥ śūraḥ syād avikatthanaḥ dātā nāpātravarṣī syāt pragalbhaḥ syād aniṣṭhuraḥ
english: Let him speak kindly without meanness; let him be brave without boasting; let him be a giver, yet not pour gifts on the unworthy; let him be bold, yet not unfeeling.

sanskrit: saṃdadhīta na cānāryair vigṛhṇīyān na bandhubhiḥ nānāptaiḥ kārayec cāraṃ kuryāt kāryam apīḍayā
english: Let him not make peace with the base, nor wage war with kinsmen; let him not employ the untrusted as his agents; let him accomplish his ends without oppression.

sanskrit: arthān brūyān na cāsatsu guṇān brūyān na cātmanaḥ ādadyān na ca sādhubhyo nāsatpuruṣam āśrayet
english: Let him not speak of his designs among the wicked, nor proclaim his own merits; let him not take from the good, nor lean upon a worthless man.

sanskrit: nāparīkṣya nayed daṇḍaṃ na ca mantraṃ prakāśayet visṛjen na ca lubdhebhyo viśvasen nāpakāriṣu
english: Let him not inflict punishment without examination, nor make his counsel known; let him not bestow upon the greedy, nor trust in those who have wronged him.

sanskrit: anīrṣur guptadāraḥ syāc cokṣaḥ syād aghṛṇī nṛpaḥ striyaṃ seveta nātyarthaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ bhuñjīta nāhitam
english: Let the king be free of envy, his wives well guarded; let him be pure, yet not squeamish; let him resort to women not overmuch, and eat what is wholesome, not what is harmful.

sanskrit: astabdhaḥ pūjayen mānyān gurūn seved amāyayā arced devān na dambhena śriyam icched akutsitām
english: Without stiffness let him honor the honorable; let him serve his elders without guile; let him worship the gods without hypocrisy, and desire only blameless prosperity.

sanskrit: seveta praṇayaṃ hitvā dakṣaḥ syān na tv akālavit sāntvayen na ca bhogārtham anugṛhṇan na cākṣipet
english: Let him serve, setting aside undue familiarity; let him be diligent, yet not a man heedless of the right time; let him conciliate, but not for the sake of enjoyment; let him favor, yet not slight.

sanskrit: praharen na tv avijñāya hatvā śatrūn na śeṣayet krodhaṃ kuryān na cākasmān mṛduḥ syān nāpakāriṣu
english: Let him not strike without due knowledge; having slain his foes, let him leave no remnant; let him not show anger without cause, nor be soft toward those who do harm.

sanskrit: evaṃ carasva rājyastho yadi śreya ihecchasi ato 'nyathā narapatir bhayam ṛcchaty anuttamam
english: Thus conduct yourself, established in your kingdom, if you desire what is good here; for acting otherwise, a lord of men comes upon peril beyond all measure.

sanskrit: iti sarvān guṇān etān yathoktān yo 'nuvartate anubhūyeha bhadrāṇi pretya svarge mahīyate
english: He who follows all these virtues as they have been told, having enjoyed blessings here, is exalted in heaven after death.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca idaṃ vacaḥ śāṃtanavasya śuśruvān; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pāṇḍavamukhyasaṃvṛtaḥ tadā vavande ca pitāmahaṃ nṛpo; yathoktam etac ca cakāra buddhimān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this discourse of the son of Śāntanu, Yudhiṣṭhira, surrounded by the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, then bowed to his grandfather, and that wise king did even as had been told.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ rājā prajā rakṣan nādhibandhena yujyate dharme ca nāparādhnoti tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How, while protecting his people, may a king not be bound by sin and not offend against dharma? Tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca samāsenaiva te tāta dharmān vakṣyāmi niścitān vistareṇa hi dharmāṇāṃ na jātv antam avāpnuyāt
english: Bhīṣma said: In brief, my son, I shall declare to you the settled duties; for of the duties told at length one could never reach the end.

sanskrit: dharmaniṣṭhāñ śrutavato vedavratasamāhitān arcitān vāsayethās tvaṃ gṛhe guṇavato dvijān
english: The twice-born who are steadfast in dharma, learned, devoted to the Vedic vows, and virtuous—honor them and lodge them in your house.

sanskrit: pratyutthāyopasaṃgṛhya caraṇāv abhivādya ca atha sarvāṇi kurvīthāḥ kāryāṇi sapurohitaḥ
english: Rising up to meet them, clasping their feet, and saluting them, you should then perform all your affairs together with your household priest.

sanskrit: dharmakāryāṇi nirvartya maṅgalāni prayujya ca brāhmaṇān vācayethās tvam arthasiddhijayāśiṣaḥ
english: Having accomplished the rites of dharma and performed the auspicious ceremonies, you should cause the Brāhmaṇas to pronounce blessings for the gaining of your ends and for victory.

sanskrit: ārjavena ca saṃpanno dhṛtyā buddhyā ca bhārata arthārthaṃ parigṛhṇīyāt kāmakrodhau ca varjayet
english: Endowed with uprightness, with firmness, and with understanding, O Bhārata, one should take up wealth for wealth's purpose, and shun desire and anger.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau puraskṛtya yo 'rthaṃ rājānutiṣṭhati na sa dharmaṃ na cāpy arthaṃ parigṛhṇāti bāliśaḥ
english: The fool who, setting desire and anger foremost, pursues wealth as a king, grasps neither dharma nor wealth.

sanskrit: mā sma lubdhāṃś ca mūrkhāṃś ca kāme cārtheṣu yūyujaḥ alubdhān buddhisaṃpannān sarvakarmasu yojayet
english: Do not employ the greedy and the foolish in matters of pleasure or of wealth; in all your tasks employ those free of greed and possessed of understanding.

sanskrit: mūrkho hy adhikṛto 'rtheṣu kāryāṇām aviśāradaḥ prajāḥ kliśnāty ayogena kāmadveṣasamanvitaḥ
english: For a fool set over affairs, unskilled in matters of business and filled with passion and spite, afflicts the people by his misconduct.

sanskrit: baliṣaṣṭhena śulkena daṇḍenāthāparādhinām śāstranītena lipsethā vetanena dhanāgamam
english: Through the sixth-part tribute, through tolls, and through the fines of offenders, and through wages, as guided by the law-books, you should seek the increase of wealth.

sanskrit: dāpayitvā karaṃ dharmyaṃ rāṣṭraṃ nityaṃ yathāvidhi aśeṣān kalpayed rājā yogakṣemān atandritaḥ
english: Having levied the lawful tax upon the realm ever according to rule, the king, unwearied, should provide for the acquiring and keeping of goods, leaving nothing undone.

sanskrit: gopāyitāraṃ dātāraṃ dharmanityam atandritam akāmadveṣasaṃyuktam anurajyanti mānavāḥ
english: The protector, the giver, ever devoted to dharma and unwearied, free from passion and spite—him men come to love.

sanskrit: mā smādharmeṇa lābhena lipsethās tvaṃ dhanāgamam dharmārthāv adhruvau tasya yo 'paśāstraparo bhavet
english: Do not seek the increase of wealth through gain won by unrighteousness; for him who follows wrong precepts, both dharma and wealth are unstable.

sanskrit: apaśāstraparo rājā saṃcayān nādhigacchati asthāne cāsya tad vittaṃ sarvam eva vinaśyati
english: A king who follows wrong precepts attains no store of wealth; and that wealth of his, ill-placed, all perishes utterly.
